explain.say: More than 2,000 years ago, Greek travellers made a must-see list of the seven most amazing things they knew. We call them the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Look at the bars: they show how tall six of them were.

explain.say: The Colossus of Rhodes, a bronze statue about 33 metres tall, as high as a ten-storey building, by a Greek harbour. It stood only about 54 years before an earthquake knocked it down. Look at the smaller bars too: a tomb, a temple and a seated statue.

faq.q: Which of the Seven Wonders still stands?
faq.a: Only the Great Pyramid of Giza, the oldest of them all, built around 2560 BCE. The other six were destroyed or are lost.

faq.q: What was the Lighthouse of Alexandria?
faq.a: A tall stone tower, perhaps about 100 metres high, built in Egypt around 280 BCE. A fire at its top guided ships, and earthquakes ruined it over many centuries.
asks: How tall was the lighthouse of Alexandria?

faq.q: How tall was the Colossus of Rhodes?
faq.a: About 33 metres, roughly as tall as the Statue of Liberty from heel to head. It stood in Rhodes, Greece, for about 54 years until an earthquake in 226 BCE.
asks: What happened to the Colossus of Rhodes?

faq.q: Did the Hanging Gardens of Babylon exist?
faq.a: Nobody is sure. No ruins have been found in Babylon, in today's Iraq, and some historians think the gardens may really have been in Nineveh, or may be a legend.

faq.q: Who made the list of Seven Wonders?
faq.a: Greek writers more than 2,000 years ago, such as the poet Antipater of Sidon, listed the wonders that travellers in their world should see.

facts: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.
The Colossus of Rhodes was about 33 metres tall and fell in an earthquake in 226 BCE.
